brief: Close the same-quant 35B NVFP4 CUDA prefill gap to vLLM on GB10 (vLLM +16.2 % at 4k, +15.9 % at 16k in gaps.md) with an fp8 W8A8 projection GEMM; profile and roofline first, gate on accuracy, opt-in until gated.
hypothesis: vLLM's CUTLASS e4m3 projection GEMM explains about 83 % of the gap (49 ms per 2048-token chunk); an e4m3 tensor-core prefill GEMM with the checkpoint's static input scales should recover it.

summary: No new GEMM was needed: the brief's fp8 W8A8 prefill projection GEMM is matmul_fp8_gemm_lt, already on main as opt-in. Re-measured against same-window vLLM (spark2, x3 interleaved): default -9.6 % / -14.0 % at 4k / 16k; lt at chunk 8192 +8.6 % / +6.4 %; decode unchanged. KL is inside the floors, but the prefix-reuse continue rows and the acc-short baseline gate fail, so lt stays opt-in and no default-on is proposed. Roofline: projections 131-143 TFLOPS with lt (54-59 % of the e4m3 roof); the routed-expert kernel is then 41-47 % of kernel time at 22-33 % of the bf16 roof.
lessons: gaps.md's prefill gap named a missing kernel that was already on main behind a flag; the real blocker is the default-on gate, not the GEMM.
Chunk size matters as much as the GEMM for the 35B: lt at chunk 2048 is +1.8 % / -3.8 % vs vLLM, at chunk 8192 +8.6 % / +6.4 %.
The post-#40 reuse judge fails lt on rows where the default is clean although lt's row-invariance test passes; a chunk-split sensitivity of e4m3 accumulation is the untested suspect.
ncu counters are not permitted on spark2 (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM): rooflines there are nsys kernel time over counted work.
After lt the grouped fp4 MoE kernel is the largest class; an in-place-accumulation experiment (+4 % end to end) costs 2-3.4x kernel rel_l2 and sits on a separate branch.
